examples.en: This snack is made from processed ingredients.
Milk is processed at a factory and then comes to the store.
Unprocessed wood is cheap.
Please check whether this photo has been edited.

examples.ko: 가공된 식품을 너무 많이 먹지 마세요.
examples.en: Do not eat too much processed food.

examples.ko: 철이 가공되면 여러 가지 물건이 돼요.
examples.en: When iron is processed, it becomes many kinds of things.

explain: '가공식품'처럼 원료에 손을 대서 바꾼 것에 써요. 사진이나 영상이 '가공되다'라고 하면 꾸며서 원래와 달라졌다는 뜻도 있어요. 손대지 않은 것은 '가공하지 않은', '날것'이라고 말해요.

phrases.en: Processed foods are often salty.
phrases.nuance_ko: '가공식품'처럼 음식에 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, used for food, as in 가공식품.

phrases.en: I want to cook with unprocessed ingredients.
phrases.nuance_ko: 손대지 않은 원래 상태를 말할 때 부정형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form describes something in its original, untouched state.

phrases.en: The photo was edited, so it looks very different from real life.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사진이나 영상을 꾸며서 달라졌을 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also used when a photo or video has been altered.

explain_en: It is used for raw material that has been worked on, as in '가공식품' (processed food). If a photo or video is '가공되다', it also means it was edited so it differs from the original. Something untouched is described as '가공하지 않은' or '날것' (raw).

en: to be involved; to be implicated

examples.ko: 이 사건에 누군가 개입된 것 같아요.
examples.en: It seems somebody was involved in this incident.

examples.ko: 제 감정이 개입되면 공정하게 판단하기 어려워요.
examples.en: If my feelings get involved, it's hard to judge fairly.
There's no evidence that the company was involved.
Be careful not to let personal reasons creep in.
Many people got involved, and things became complicated.
The more human hands get involved, the more the result changes.

explain: '끼어들다'는 대화나 줄에 끼는 일상적인 말이고, '개입되다'는 어떤 일에 다른 사람이나 요소가 들어와 영향을 주는 것이에요. 좋은 일보다는 문제가 되는 일에 많이 써요.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 이 일에 깊이 개입돼 있어요.
phrases.en: He is deeply involved in this matter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 일에 많이 관련되어 있다는 뜻이고, 보통 문제가 되는 일에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means being heavily involved, usually in a problematic matter.

phrases.example: 이 일에는 제 의견이 개입되지 않았어요.
phrases.en: My opinion was not involved in this.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 써서 '관련이 없다, 영향을 주지 않았다'고 말할 때 좋아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Negative form, used to say something had no involvement or influence.

phrases.example: 이 사건에는 여러 회사가 개입되어 있어요.
phrases.en: Several companies are involved in this case.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 어떤 상태로 관련되어 있다는 뜻이고, 뉴스에서 많이 들어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the current state of being involved; common in the news.

explain_en: '끼어들다' is the everyday word for cutting into a conversation or a line. '개입되다' is when a person or factor enters a matter and affects it, more often in problematic situations than good ones.

en: to be related; to be connected

examples.ko: 이 문제는 돈 문제와 결부돼 있어요.
examples.en: This problem is tied to money matters.
Might the two incidents be connected?
Health is deeply linked to lifestyle habits.
Happiness isn't tied only to success.
When it's linked to grades, students get more nervous.

examples.ko: 이 정책은 환경 문제와 결부돼서 논란이 커졌어요.
examples.en: This policy got linked with environmental issues and the controversy grew.

explain: 'A는 B와 결부되다'처럼 '와/과'를 써요. '연결되다'가 실제로 이어지는 느낌이라면 '결부되다'는 서로 관계가 있다고 묶여 보이는 느낌이에요. '관련되다', '연관되다'와 비슷해요.

phrases.example: 이 사건은 그 회사와 관련돼 있어요.
phrases.en: This case is related to that company.
phrases.nuance_ko: '결부되다'보다 쉽고 널리 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier and more widely used word than '결부되다'.

phrases.en: Problems tied to money are hard to solve.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ'을 붙여 어떤 일과 묶여 있는 문제를 꾸며 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The '-ㄴ' form describes an issue that is bound up with something else.

phrases.en: The two problems are tied to each other.
phrases.nuance_ko: '서로'를 넣어 두 가지가 맞물려 있다는 뜻을 분명히 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '서로' makes it clear that the two things are interlinked.
phrases.en_equiv: to be tied to each other

explain_en: It takes '와/과', as in 'A는 B와 결부되다'. While '연결되다' feels like things are actually joined, '결부되다' feels like two things are seen as bound together by a relationship. It is close to '관련되다' and '연관되다'.

p.n: 결부되다 means closely bound up with something; 관련되다 only says there is a relation.

en: to be united; to be combined

examples.en: The two parts are firmly joined together.
When oxygen and hydrogen combine, they become water.
It's a design that combines tradition and modernity.

examples.ko: 여러 기술이 결합돼서 새 제품이 나왔어요.
examples.en: Several technologies were combined to produce a new product.
I bought a toy where blocks join together.
Different kinds of music sometimes get combined.

explain: 따로 있던 둘 이상이 하나로 붙을 때 써요. 부품, 화학 물질, 기술, 문화처럼 글과 설명에서 자주 나와요. '합쳐지다'는 더 일상적이고, '섞이다'는 형태가 사라지고 뒤섞일 때 써요.

phrases.en: The two companies combined their technology.
phrases.nuance_ko: '결합되다'의 능동형으로, 합치는 쪽이 주어예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The active form; the one combining is the subject.

phrases.en: The two rivers join here.
phrases.nuance_ko: '결합되다'보다 일상적이고 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: More everyday and easier than 결합되다.

phrases.en: The combination of music and dance is great.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서로 다른 둘이 하나로 만나는 것을 명사로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun for two different things coming together as one.

explain_en: For two or more separate things becoming one: parts, chemicals, technologies, cultures. Common in writing and explanations. '합쳐지다' is the everyday version, and '섞이다' is for things that mix and lose their shape.

dis.h: parts or elements joined into one

p.n: 연합 is for groups or countries allying, not for parts of an object.

examples.en: Twins can't be told apart by their faces alone.
These two words are distinguished by pronunciation.
I marked them so they can be told apart by color.
I wish the real and the fake could be easily told apart.

examples.ko: 그 가게는 다른 곳과 확실히 구별되는 맛이 있어요.
examples.en: That shop has a taste that is clearly distinct from other places.

examples.ko: 크기로 구별된 상자들이 줄지어 놓여 있어요.
examples.en: Boxes distinguished by size are lined up in a row.

explain: '구분되다'와 거의 같이 쓰지만, '구별'은 다른 점을 알아본다는 느낌이 강하고 '구분'은 기준에 따라 나눈다는 느낌이 강해요. '쌍둥이를 구별하다', '쓰레기를 구분하다'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.example: 저는 두 소리를 구별할 수 없어요.
phrases.en: I can't tell the two sounds apart.
phrases.nuance_ko: 능동형으로, 다른 점을 알아보는 사람이 주어일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The active form, with the person telling them apart as the subject.

phrases.en: I can't tell the twins apart.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷해서 차이를 모를 때 일상에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Common in daily talk when things look too alike to tell apart.

phrases.en: This book is divided into two parts.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기준에 따라 나뉠 때 더 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits better when things are divided by a standard.

explain_en: It overlaps with 구분되다, but 구별 leans toward noticing differences while 구분 leans toward dividing by a standard. '쌍둥이를 구별하다' and '쓰레기를 구분하다' sound more natural.

en: to be rescued; to be saved

examples.ko: 산에서 길을 잃은 사람이 무사히 구출되었어요.
examples.en: A person lost in the mountains was rescued safely.
The child was rescued from the burning building.
The rescued puppy met a new family.

examples.ko: 갇혀 있던 사람들이 하루 만에 구출될 수 있었어요.
examples.en: The people who were trapped could be rescued within a day.

examples.ko: 배에 있던 승객이 모두 구출돼서 안심했어요.
examples.en: I felt relieved that all the passengers on the ship were rescued.
The moment they were rescued from danger, everyone cheered.

explain: 구출되다는 위험하거나 갇힌 곳에서 도움을 받아 빠져나올 때 써요. 사고, 화재, 납치처럼 급한 상황이 떠오르는 말이에요. '구조되다'는 재난에서 도움을 받는 쪽에, 구출되다는 갇힌 곳에서 빼내지는 쪽에 가까운데 실제로는 거의 겹쳐서 써요.

phrases.en: Everyone on the boat was rescued.
phrases.nuance_ko: '구출되다'와 가깝지만 재난에서 도움을 받는 쪽에 더 가까워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Close to 구출되다 but leans toward being helped out of a disaster.

phrases.en: The trapped people were rescued safely.
phrases.nuance_ko: '무사히'와 함께 쓰면 다치지 않고 나왔다는 뜻이 분명해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 무사히, it clearly means they came out unharmed.

phrases.en: The child waited to be rescued.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-기를 기다리다'로 아직 구출되지 않은 상황을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With -기를 기다리다, it describes a situation where rescue hasn't happened yet.

explain_en: 구출되다 is used when someone gets out of a dangerous or confined place with help. It brings to mind urgent situations such as accidents, fires or kidnappings. 구조되다 leans toward being helped in a disaster and 구출되다 toward being pulled out of confinement, but in practice they overlap a lot.

dis.h: rescued out of captivity or a trapped place

p.n: 구조 is possible but sounds like a rescue operation. 구출 stresses being freed from the kidnappers.

en: to be confined to; to be restricted to a narrow scope

examples.ko: 이 문제는 우리 학교에만 국한되지 않아요.
examples.en: This problem is not limited to our school.
The story is limited to a single topic.
Participation in the event will be limited to students.

examples.ko: 그 인기는 어린이에게만 국한되는 것이 아니에요.
examples.en: That popularity is not limited to children.

examples.ko: 우리 회사의 고민은 비용에 국한되어 있지 않아요.
examples.en: My company's worries are not confined to cost.
The conversation was limited to work talk, so it was boring.

explain: '~에 국한되다'처럼 범위를 나타내는 '~에'와 같이 써요. '~뿐이다', '~에 한하다'와 비슷하지만 글이나 발표에서 더 자주 나와요. '~에 국한되지 않다'가 특히 많아요.

phrases.en: This problem is not limited to children.
phrases.nuance_ko: 범위가 그보다 넓다고 말할 때 가장 자주 쓰는 꼴이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common form, used to say the scope is wider than that.

phrases.example: 이 규칙은 회사 안에 국한돼 있어요.
phrases.en: This rule is limited to inside the company.
phrases.nuance_ko: 범위가 이미 좁게 정해져 있는 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a state where the scope is already narrowly fixed.

phrases.example: 이 할인은 회원에 한해 받을 수 있어요.
phrases.en: This discount is available only to members.
phrases.nuance_ko: '국한되다'와 비슷한 뜻이고 안내문이나 규칙에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Close in meaning to 국한되다 and common in notices and rules.

explain_en: It pairs with 에 to show the range, as in ~에 국한되다. It is close to ~뿐이다 or ~에 한하다, but appears more in writing and presentations. The negative ~에 국한되지 않다 is especially common.

dis.h: confined to one narrow area only

p.n: 국한 means confined within a boundary; 한정 simply sets the range.

examples.ko: 선수는 징계로 한 달간 근신 처분을 받았어요.
examples.en: The player received a one-month suspension as discipline.

examples.ko: 사고를 친 뒤 그는 집에서 근신 중이에요.
examples.en: After causing trouble, he is keeping a low profile at home.

examples.ko: 논란이 커지자 그 연예인은 한동안 근신에 들어갔어요.
examples.en: As the controversy grew, the celebrity went into lying low for a while.

examples.ko: 시험 기간에는 놀러 가지 않고 근신 모드로 지내요.
examples.en: During exams I stay in lie-low mode and don't go out to have fun.

examples.ko: 근신 기간이 끝나면 다시 경기에 나갈 수 있어요.
examples.en: Once the suspension period ends, he can play in matches again.

examples.ko: 교장 선생님은 규칙을 어긴 학생들에게 근신을 지시했어요.
examples.en: The principal ordered the students who broke the rules to serve a period of self-restraint.

explain: 학교나 회사, 스포츠에서 '근신 처분'처럼 징계의 하나로 많이 나와요. 스스로 조용히 지내며 조심한다는 뜻으로도 쓰여서 '요즘 근신 중이에요'라고 가볍게 말하기도 해요. 마음을 뉘우치는 '반성'과는 달리, 행동을 조심하며 지낸다는 쪽에 가까워요.

phrases.example: 근신 기간이 끝나면 다시 경기에 나올 수 있어요.
phrases.en: Once the suspension period ends, he can play in games again.
phrases.nuance_ko: 징계로 조심하며 지내야 하는 기간을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The period one must lie low as a disciplinary measure.

phrases.example: 그 연예인은 논란 후 근신에 들어갔어요.
phrases.en: After the controversy, the celebrity went into lying low.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조용히 지내기 시작한다는 뜻의 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pair meaning one starts keeping a low profile.

phrases.example: 요즘 자숙 중이라 모임에 안 나가요.
phrases.en: I'm keeping a low profile these days, so I'm skipping gatherings.
phrases.nuance_ko: '근신'과 비슷하게 스스로 조심하며 지낸다는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 근신: carefully behaving on one's own.

explain_en: It often appears as a form of discipline in schools, companies and sports, as in '근신 처분'. It is also used for quietly keeping oneself in check, so people can say '요즘 근신 중이에요' lightly. Unlike '반성' (reflecting with regret), it leans toward behaving carefully.

examples.en: The puppy didn't want to walk and was dragged along.

examples.ko: 친구에게 끌려와서 원하지 않는 모임에 왔어요.
examples.en: My friend dragged me here, and now I'm at a gathering I don't want to be at.

examples.ko: 아이가 엄마 손에 끌려와서 병원에 왔어요.
examples.en: The child was pulled along by his mom's hand to the hospital.
A big fish was reeled in on the fishing line.
When I pull the rope, the box comes toward me.
You look like someone who was dragged here against your will.

explain: 자기 뜻과 상관없이 누군가에게 이끌려 오는 느낌이 강해요. 그래서 '억지로 끌려오다'처럼 쓰는 경우가 많아요. 내가 직접 끌고 오는 것은 '끌고 오다'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 숙제가 많은 날 학원에 억지로 끌려왔어요.
phrases.en: I was dragged to the academy against my will on a day with lots of homework.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원하지 않는데 따라온다는 뜻이 분명해지는 가장 자연스러운 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most natural collocation; makes it clear you came unwillingly.

phrases.en: I was dragged here by my friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거형으로 '누구에게 끌려왔다'라고 이유를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Past form, used to say who dragged you here.

phrases.example: 저는 아무에게도 끌려오지 않았어요. 제가 직접 왔어요.
phrases.en: I wasn't dragged here by anyone. I came on my own.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스스로 온 것이라고 말할 때 부정형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Negative form, used to say you came of your own will.

explain_en: It carries a strong feeling of being pulled along against your own will, so it often appears as '억지로 끌려오다'. When you pull something here yourself, you say '끌고 오다'.

examples.ko: 뉴스에서 불법 어선 나포 소식을 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw the news about the seizure of an illegal fishing boat.

examples.ko: 해경은 불법 조업 선박의 나포를 결정했어요.
examples.en: The coast guard decided to seize the illegal fishing vessel.
Right after the seizure, the captain was questioned.

examples.ko: 어선이 나포되면서 두 나라 사이가 불편해졌어요.
examples.en: Relations between the two countries became tense when the fishing boat was seized.

examples.ko: 그 배가 나포된 이유가 아직 확실하지 않아요.
examples.en: The reason that ship was seized is still not clear.

examples.ko: 그 배는 나포 사흘 만에 풀려났어요.
examples.en: The ship was released three days after its seizure.

explain: 주로 배나 비행기를 붙잡을 때 쓰고, 뉴스에서 많이 나와요. 사람을 잡을 때는 보통 '체포'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 불법 어선 나포 뉴스가 자주 나와요.
phrases.en: News about seizing illegal fishing boats comes out often.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The pairing most often used in news.

phrases.en: The coast guard started a capture operation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 붙잡으려는 계획이나 행동을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a plan or action to capture something.

phrases.en: A suspicious ship was captured at sea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 붙잡힌 쪽을 주어로 말할 때 쓰는 피동 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A passive form used when the captured thing is the subject.

explain_en: It is mostly used for seizing ships or aircraft and often appears in the news. For catching a person, people usually say '체포' (arrest).

en: to be caught; to be hooked

examples.en: Three crucian carp were caught today.

examples.ko: 광고 제목에 낚여서 영상을 끝까지 봤어요.
examples.en: I got hooked by the ad title and watched the video to the end.

examples.ko: 자극적인 기사 제목에 낚이지 않게 조심하세요.
examples.en: Be careful not to be lured by sensational headlines.
Before I knew it, I fell for my friend's prank.

examples.ko: 낚였다는 걸 알고 나서 웃음이 나왔어요.
examples.en: After realizing I'd been tricked, I laughed.
Fish are easily caught with this bait.

explain: 물고기가 잡힌다는 뜻 외에, 요즘은 자극적인 제목에 속아서 클릭했을 때 '낚였다'고 말해요. 가볍고 장난스러운 입말이라 공식적인 글에는 잘 안 써요.

phrases.en: Don't get hooked by titles like this.
phrases.nuance_ko: 속지 말라고 가볍게 충고할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual warning not to be fooled.

phrases.example: 아, 또 낚였어! 내용이 하나도 없네.
phrases.en: Ah, I got fooled again! There's no content at all.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반말이라 친구끼리 편하게 속았다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Casual speech used among friends to say you were tricked.

phrases.en: Fish are caught easily in the morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비유가 아니라 실제로 물고기가 잡힌다는 본래 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The literal meaning: fish actually being caught.

explain_en: Besides a fish being caught, people nowadays say '낚였다' when they were fooled into clicking on a sensational title. It is light, playful spoken language and is not used much in formal writing.

examples.en: Old relics had been buried underground.

examples.ko: 그 지역에는 석유가 많이 매장돼 있어요.
examples.en: There are large oil reserves in that region.
An ancient city was buried under volcanic ash.
I watched a movie about finding buried treasure.
They're surveying the places where resources lie underground.
The documents were found before being buried.

explain: 땅속에 묻혀 있을 때 써요. 유물·자원·보물처럼 파내야 찾을 수 있는 것에 많이 써요. 가게 뜻의 '매장(賣場)'과는 소리만 같고 완전히 다른 말이에요.

phrases.en: The treasure is buried underground.
phrases.nuance_ko: '매장되다'의 쉬운 말로, 일상에서 훨씬 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier word for '매장되다', much more common in daily speech.

phrases.en: This country has large oil reserves.
phrases.nuance_ko: 땅속에 묻혀 있는 자원의 양을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the amount of a resource underground.

phrases.en: There is gold buried in this mountain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자원이 땅속에 있는 상태를 말할 때 '-아/어 있다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '-아/어 있다' to describe resources lying underground.

explain_en: For things lying underground: relics, resources, treasure that must be dug up. It only sounds like '매장' meaning 'store' (賣場); the two are different words.

dis.h: dead or deposits buried underground; formal

examples.ko: 인터넷에서 그 가수가 뭇매를 맞고 있어요.
examples.en: That singer is getting hammered with criticism online.

examples.ko: 잘못된 발언으로 정치인이 여론의 뭇매를 맞았어요.
examples.en: The politician was lashed by public opinion over his wrong remarks.

examples.ko: 광고가 논란이 되어 회사가 뭇매를 맞았어요.
examples.en: The ad caused controversy, and the company took a lot of heat.
I apologized honestly, ready to take the heat.

examples.ko: 그 발표는 비판의 뭇매를 피하지 못했어요.
examples.en: That announcement couldn't avoid a barrage of criticism.
Under the pile-on from people, he finally apologized.

explain: 거의 '뭇매를 맞다' 형태로 써요. 원래는 여러 사람이 한꺼번에 때리는 매를 뜻하고, 뉴스에서는 '여론의 뭇매'처럼 비판이 한꺼번에 쏟아지는 상황에 비유해서 써요.

phrases.example: 광고 논란으로 그 회사가 뭇매를 맞았어요.
phrases.en: get hammered with criticism
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 사람에게 한꺼번에 심한 비난을 받을 때 써요. 뉴스나 인터넷 기사에 많아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when many people criticize someone harshly at once; common in news and online articles.

explain_en: It is almost always used as '뭇매를 맞다'. Originally it means a beating from many people at once, and in the news it is used figuratively, as in '여론의 뭇매', for criticism pouring in all at once.

examples.ko: 세관에서 불법 물품 밀반입을 단속하고 있어요.
examples.en: Customs is cracking down on the smuggling of illegal goods.
Smuggling animals and plants into the country is prohibited by law.

examples.ko: 밀반입 혐의로 조사를 받았다는 뉴스를 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw a news report that someone was investigated on suspicion of smuggling.

examples.ko: 밀반입 사실이 알려지면서 큰 문제가 됐어요.
examples.en: It became a big problem once the smuggling came to light.

examples.ko: 국경 지역에서는 밀반입이 자주 문제가 돼요.
examples.en: Smuggling is often a problem in border areas.

examples.ko: 세관 직원은 밀반입 경로를 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: The customs officer is looking for the smuggling route.

explain: 정식으로 신고하고 들여오는 '수입'과 달리, 법을 어기고 몰래 들여오는 것을 말해요. 반대로 몰래 내보내는 것은 '밀반출'이에요. '밀수'와 가깝지만 '밀반입'은 들여오는 쪽만 가리켜요.

phrases.en: He was caught at the airport smuggling in a banned item.
phrases.nuance_ko: '밀반입'의 동사형이라 행동을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the verb form of 밀반입, used to describe the act.

phrases.en: Airports check bags to prevent smuggling.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세관이나 정부가 단속하는 일을 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is a common phrase for customs or governments cracking down.

phrases.en: A drug smuggling case was in the news.
phrases.nuance_ko: '밀반입'은 몰래 들여오는 것만 가리키고, '밀수'는 몰래 들여오거나 내보내는 일 전체를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: 밀반입 refers only to bringing goods in secretly, while 밀수 covers smuggling in either direction.

explain_en: Unlike '수입' (import through proper channels), this means secretly bringing something in against the law. The opposite, secretly taking something out, is '밀반출'. It is close to '밀수', but '밀반입' only refers to the bringing-in side.

en: to be straightened; to be adjusted

examples.en: The wrong information was corrected belatedly.

examples.ko: 오랜 습관이 한 달 만에 바로잡혔어요.
examples.en: My long-standing habit was fixed in a month.
Once your posture is corrected, back pain decreases.
I'm glad the misunderstanding was cleared up through talking.
The bent wire doesn't straighten out easily.

examples.ko: 잘못이 바로잡힐 때까지 계속 요구할 거예요.
examples.en: I'll keep demanding it until the mistake is corrected.

explain: '바로잡다'의 피동형으로, 잘못이나 비뚤어진 것이 고쳐지는 결과에 초점이 있어요. 사람이 고치는 상황은 '바로잡다', 저절로 또는 누군가에 의해 고쳐지는 상황은 '바로잡히다'를 써요. 오류, 자세, 질서, 오해와 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: The misunderstanding was cleared up as we talked.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잘못 알았던 것이 올바르게 고쳐진다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means something misunderstood gets corrected.

phrases.en: My posture got corrected after I exercised.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비뚤어진 몸의 상태가 바르게 되는 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a crooked body position becoming straight.

phrases.en: All the wrong parts have been fixed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더 쉽고 일반적인 말이에요. '바로잡히다'는 올바르게 된다는 느낌이 더 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simpler, more general word; 바로잡히다 stresses being set right.

explain_en: This is the passive form of '바로잡다' and focuses on the result of something wrong being fixed. When someone fixes it, use '바로잡다'; when it gets fixed, use '바로잡히다'. It fits errors, posture, order and misunderstandings.

examples.en: My uncle raises cattle.
This animal is hard to keep at home.
Animals are healthy only if the raising environment is good.
The zookeeper feeds the animals every morning.

examples.ko: 야생 동물의 사육은 법으로 정해져 있어요.
examples.en: The raising of wild animals is regulated by law.

examples.ko: 닭 사육 농장이 마을 끝에 있어요.
examples.en: The chicken farm is at the end of the village.

explain: '사육'은 사람이 동물을 먹이고 기르는 일이에요. 반려동물은 보통 '키우다'라고 하고, 농장이나 동물원처럼 일로 기를 때 '사육'을 써서 조금 사무적인 느낌이 나요. 식물은 '재배'라고 해요.

phrases.en: This village is famous for raising livestock.
phrases.nuance_ko: 농장에서 동물을 기르는 일을 말할 때 가장 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for farm animal raising.

phrases.en: There are a hundred chickens in the breeding pen.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동물을 기르는 장소를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The place where animals are raised.

phrases.en: My uncle raises pigs in the countryside.
phrases.nuance_ko: '사육'에 '하다'를 붙여 일로 기른다는 뜻을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 하다 shows raising animals as work.

explain_en: 사육 is humans feeding and raising animals. For pets people say '키우다', while 사육 is used for farms and zoos where it is work, so it sounds somewhat businesslike. For plants the word is '재배'.

examples.ko: 그 광고는 세뇌처럼 계속 머릿속에 남아요.
examples.en: That ad stays in my head like brainwashing.

examples.ko: 어릴 때부터 받은 세뇌에서 벗어나기는 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: It's not easy to break free from indoctrination received since childhood.
The repeating song is almost at the level of brainwashing.

examples.ko: 그는 이상한 단체의 세뇌 교육을 받았다고 말했어요.
examples.en: He said he received indoctrination training from a strange group.

examples.ko: 영화 속 악당이 주인공에게 세뇌를 시도해요.
examples.en: The villain in the movie tries to brainwash the hero.

examples.ko: 매일 같은 말을 들으니까 세뇌가 되는 것 같아요.
examples.en: Hearing the same words every day, it feels like I'm being brainwashed.

explain: 원래는 사상이나 생각을 강제로 바꾸는 무거운 말이지만, 요즘은 노래나 광고가 머릿속에서 안 떠나는 걸 가볍게 '세뇌당했어요', '세뇌됐어요'라고 농담처럼 말하기도 해요. '세뇌하다', '세뇌되다'와 함께 쓰여요. 진지한 상황과 장난스러운 상황을 말투로 구분하면 돼요.

phrases.en: I've been brainwashed by that song because I kept hearing it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남이 나를 세뇌했다는 느낌이고, 농담으로도 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means someone or something brainwashed you; often used jokingly.

phrases.example: 광고를 자꾸 봐서 나도 모르게 세뇌됐어요.
phrases.en: I got brainwashed without realizing it from seeing the ad so often.
phrases.nuance_ko: '세뇌당하다'보다 결과를 담담하게 말하는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Sounds more neutral than 세뇌당하다, focusing on the result.

phrases.en: That kind of indoctrination is dangerous.
phrases.nuance_ko: 생각을 강제로 바꾸는 교육을 비판할 때 쓰는 무거운 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A heavy collocation used to criticize education that forces beliefs on people.

explain_en: It originally means forcibly changing someone's thoughts or beliefs, a heavy word, but these days people also joke about a song or ad stuck in their head with '세뇌당했어요' or '세뇌됐어요'. It is used with '세뇌하다' and '세뇌되다'. You can tell the serious and playful uses apart by tone and context.

en: to be damaged; to be harmed

examples.en: The book was damaged because it got rained on.
The old painting was damaged by sunlight.
Please send a photo of the damaged part.

examples.ko: 상자가 손상되면 환불을 받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: If the box is damaged, you can get a refund.
My hair was damaged and split, so I went to the salon.

examples.ko: 손상되는 일이 없도록 포장을 두껍게 했어요.
examples.en: I wrapped it thickly so it would not get damaged.

explain: '망가지다'는 물건이 못 쓰게 됐을 때 일상에서 쓰고, '손상되다'는 조금 다치거나 상한 것에도 써요. 물건뿐 아니라 '명예가 손상되다', '이미지가 손상되다'처럼 눈에 안 보이는 것에도 써요. 기계가 안 움직일 때는 '고장 나다'를 써요.

phrases.en: We replace damaged items.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조금 다치거나 상한 물건을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this for items that are slightly damaged or spoiled.

phrases.example: 소문 때문에 그 사람의 명예가 손상됐어요.
phrases.en: His reputation was damaged because of the rumor.
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈에 안 보이는 것에도 쓰는 대표 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is a typical pairing for things you can't see.

phrases.en: I'm glad the box wasn't damaged.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상하지 않고 그대로라는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This means something stayed intact without damage.

explain_en: '망가지다' is the everyday word for something that can no longer be used, while '손상되다' also covers slight damage. It applies to things you cannot see too, as in '명예가 손상되다' and '이미지가 손상되다'. For a machine that does not work, use '고장 나다'.

dis.h: get damaged or harmed, even partly

p.n: 훼손되다 is more formal and suggests defacing or harm to something valued.

examples.ko: 내부 갈등 때문에 조직이 와해 위기에 놓였어요.
examples.en: Because of internal conflict, the organization faces a breakup crisis.
The coach tried to keep the team from falling apart.

examples.ko: 가족의 와해가 사회 문제로 이어지기도 해요.
examples.en: The breakdown of families sometimes leads to social problems.

examples.ko: 그 회사는 노조 와해 의혹으로 논란이 됐어요.
examples.en: The company drew controversy over suspicions of undermining the union.
The collapse of trust can happen in an instant.

examples.ko: 인기 그룹이 와해로 이어질 만한 분쟁에 휘말렸어요.
examples.en: The popular group got caught up in a dispute that could lead to its breakup.

explain: 조직, 체제, 관계가 무너져 흩어지는 것을 말해요. '와해 위기', '와해를 막다'처럼 쓰고, 동사로는 '와해되다', '와해시키다'가 있어요. '붕괴'는 건물처럼 물리적인 것에도 쓰지만 '와해'는 주로 조직이나 관계에 써요.

phrases.en: The breakup of the organization started from a small distrust.
phrases.nuance_ko: '와해' 앞에 무엇이 무너지는지 넣어 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put what is falling apart before '와해' to say exactly what collapsed.

phrases.en: A small quarrel led to the team's breakup.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 일이 결과적으로 무너짐이 될 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when something ends up causing a collapse.

phrases.example: 모두가 힘을 모아 모임의 와해를 막았어요.
phrases.en: Everyone joined forces and prevented the group from breaking up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무너지기 전에 지키려는 노력을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for efforts to protect something before it falls apart.

explain_en: It means an organization, system or relationship collapsing and scattering. It is used as '와해 위기' and '와해를 막다', and the verbs are '와해되다' and '와해시키다'. '붕괴' can also describe physical things like buildings, but '와해' is mainly for organizations and relationships.

examples.en: I had finger amputation surgery after an accident.

examples.ko: 절단 부위에 감염이 생기지 않게 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: You must be careful not to get an infection at the amputation site.

examples.ko: 철근 절단 작업은 위험해서 장갑을 꼭 껴요.
examples.en: Cutting rebar is dangerous, so I always wear gloves.

examples.ko: 전선 절단 때문에 마을 전체가 정전됐어요.
examples.en: The whole village lost power because a wire was cut.

examples.ko: 절단 위기를 넘기고 다리를 지킬 수 있었어요.
examples.en: He got past the risk of amputation and was able to keep his leg.

examples.ko: 이 기계는 절단 속도가 아주 빨라요.
examples.en: This machine cuts very fast.

explain: 절단은 '자르다'보다 딱딱한 말이라서 의료·공사·사고 뉴스에 많이 나와요. 몸의 일부를 잘라 내는 일이나 금속·전선을 끊는 일에 써요. 빵이나 종이처럼 가벼운 것에는 '자르다'를 써요.

phrases.en: He had an amputation surgery on his leg.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸의 일부를 잘라 내는 수술을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for surgery that removes part of the body.

phrases.en: An accident in which a body part was cut off happened at the factory.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기계 때문에 몸의 일부가 잘리는 사고를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: An accident in which a body part is cut off, often by a machine.

phrases.en: I cut the steel plate with a cutter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 단단한 것을 자르는 기계나 도구예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A machine or tool for cutting hard materials.

explain_en: 절단 is a stiffer word than '자르다' and appears in medical, construction and accident news: cutting off a body part, or cutting metal or wire. For bread or paper, Koreans just say '자르다'.

examples.en: Air expands when it is heated.

examples.ko: 우주는 빅뱅 이후 계속 팽창되어 왔어요.
examples.en: The universe has kept expanding since the Big Bang.
The balloon swelled too much and burst.

examples.ko: 인구 증가로 도시가 팽창되면서 교통 문제가 생겼어요.
examples.en: As the city expanded because of population growth, traffic problems appeared.

examples.ko: 금속이 열에 팽창되는 정도는 재료마다 달라요.
examples.en: How much metal expands with heat differs by material.
Please explain why the budget swelled.

explain: '팽창하다'가 더 자주 쓰여요. '팽창되다'는 열이나 압력 같은 힘을 받아 부풀어 커진다는 피동의 느낌이 있어요. 반대말은 '수축되다'예요. 과학 글과 뉴스에서 만나고, 일상에서 부풀 때는 '부풀다', '커지다'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: Air expands when it receives heat.
phrases.nuance_ko: '팽창되다'보다 더 자주 쓰는 말로, 스스로 커지는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: More common than 팽창되다; describes something growing larger on its own.

phrases.en: The balloon got bigger and bigger when air was put in.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요. 과학적인 느낌은 없어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simple everyday word without a scientific feel.

phrases.en: When it gets cold, air contracts.
phrases.nuance_ko: '팽창되다'의 반대말로, 함께 묶어서 자주 배워요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 팽창되다; the two are often learned together.

explain_en: 팽창하다 is the more common form. 팽창되다 has a passive feel: something swells or grows because of a force such as heat or pressure. Its opposite is 수축되다. It appears in science writing and news; in daily life, 부풀다 or 커지다 sounds more natural.

dis.h: swell in volume, like gas or economy

p.n: 확장 does not describe gas swelling.

examples.en: The police encirclement gradually tightened.
The army lifted the siege of the city and withdrew.
The encirclement operation continued all night.

examples.ko: 적의 포위를 뚫고 나온 이야기가 영화로 만들어졌어요.
examples.en: The story of breaking through the enemy encirclement was made into a movie.
I heard they held out for three days under siege.
Many personnel were sent to surround the building.

explain: 포위는 사방을 빙 둘러싸서 빠져나가지 못하게 하는 일이에요. 군대·경찰·사냥 이야기에서 자주 나오고, '포위를 풀다', '포위를 뚫다'처럼 써요. 일상에서 사람들이 빙 둘러싸는 건 '둘러싸다'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.example: 선수가 상대 팀의 포위를 뚫고 달렸어요.
phrases.en: The player broke through the other team's encirclement and ran.
phrases.nuance_ko: 둘러싼 사람들 사이로 빠져나갈 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase for breaking out through those surrounding you.

phrases.en: The police gradually tightened the cordon.
phrases.nuance_ko: 둘러싼 범위를 그물처럼 말하는 단어로, 뉴스에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the surrounding ring like a net, common in news.

phrases.en: The army began an encirclement operation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 군대나 경찰이 계획해서 둘러싸는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: An organized plan by the army or police to surround something.

explain_en: 포위 is surrounding on all sides so nothing can escape, common in military, police and hunting stories, as in '포위를 풀다' (lift the siege) and '포위를 뚫다' (break through). For people simply crowding around, '둘러싸다' is more natural.

examples.ko: 사고 현장에서 부상자의 후송이 바로 시작됐어요.
examples.en: At the accident scene, the transfer of the injured began right away.
A helicopter is the fastest way to transfer a patient.
The patient's condition got worse during the transfer.
The doctor decided to transfer the patient to a big hospital.

examples.ko: 응급 후송 차량 때문에 길이 잠깐 막혔어요.
examples.en: The road was blocked for a moment because of an emergency transport vehicle.
On an island, evacuation is difficult when the weather is bad.

explain: '이송'과 비슷하지만, 후송은 전쟁터나 사고·재난 현장에서 다친 사람을 더 안전한 곳이나 큰 병원으로 옮길 때 많이 써요. 병원끼리 환자를 옮길 때는 '이송'이 더 자연스러워요. 일상 대화에서는 '병원으로 옮기다'라고 말해요.

phrases.en: There is a patient who needs emergency evacuation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 급하게 다친 사람을 옮겨야 할 때 '긴급'과 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '긴급' when an injured person must be moved urgently.

phrases.en: The injured are waiting for evacuation at the scene.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옮겨지기 전의 상황을 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing for describing the situation before being moved.

phrases.example: 부상자에 대한 후송 조치가 바로 이루어졌어요.
phrases.en: Evacuation measures for the injured were taken right away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스나 보고에서 쓰는 격식 있는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal phrase used in news and reports.

explain_en: It is similar to '이송' (transfer), but 후송 is often used when an injured person is moved from an accident, disaster or battle site to a safer place or a bigger hospital. When patients are moved between hospitals, '이송' sounds more natural. In daily talk people say '병원으로 옮기다'.

en: to be trained; to be drilled; to be exercised

examples.ko: 이 개는 잘 훈련돼서 말을 잘 들어요.
examples.en: This dog is well trained, so it listens well.
The players are trained hard every day.
A trained staff member will guide you.
It's dangerous if you aren't trained enough.
Once your body is trained, it's less tiring.
The soldiers were trained strictly.

explain: 사람이나 동물이 훈련을 받아 몸에 익은 상태예요. 스스로 연습하는 것은 '훈련하다', 시켜서 하게 하는 것은 '훈련시키다'로 나눠요. '훈련된 개'처럼 꾸미는 말로 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 훈련된 개는 주인의 말을 잘 들어요.
phrases.en: A trained dog listens well to its owner.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸밀 때 쓰는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form used to modify a noun that follows.

phrases.en: These employees are well trained.
phrases.nuance_ko: 훈련이 끝나 몸에 익은 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe a state in which training is done and the skill has been learned.

phrases.en: This puppy hasn't been trained yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아직 훈련을 못 받았다는 뜻의 부정형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative form meaning training has not happened yet.

explain_en: It describes a person or animal that has gone through training and has the skill. Doing it yourself is 훈련하다, and making someone else do it is 훈련시키다. It often shows up as a modifier, like 훈련된 개.

p.n: 양성되다 is for people raised as professionals, not animals.
